register_agent.description: Join the hub at the start of your work, before taking locks or tasks: returns who else is active, which files are locked and recent changes. Pass worktree_root when you work in your own git worktree.

parent_id.description: Parent agent ID if this is a spawned sub-agent (omit for root agents)

graph_agent_id.description: ID in the coordination graph this agent implements (e.g. 'planner'; omit if not graph-mapped)

worktree_root.description: Worktree root path (omit to inherit project root)

heartbeat.description: Call between steps (every 30 s to a few minutes, and before and after a long build or test run). It keeps you listed as active and renews your locks that have less than half their TTL left, so a lock lasts as long as you keep heartbeating. The reply lists locks_renewed, locks_expiring (will run out before the next heartbeat) and locks_expired (ran out before a heartbeat could renew them: acquire_lock again). A heartbeat brings back an agent the reaper marked stale (revived: true).

deregister_agent.description: Call when your work is finished. Releases your locks (locks_released counts the ones still held; locks_expired lists those whose TTL had already run out), hands your children to your parent and frees the coordinator lease.

list_agents.description: See who else is working on the project now. By default it hides agents without a heartbeat for stale_timeout seconds; stale_hidden and hint then name them (often busy in a long build). active_only=false lists every agent ever registered.

stale_timeout.description: Seconds after which an agent is considered stale

get_agent_relations.description: Find your parent and children (mode='lineage') or the agents that share your parent (mode='siblings'), for example to decide whom to message.

acquire_lock.description: Before editing a file other agents may also edit (shared modules, lib.rs, Cargo.toml), lock it so nobody overwrites your change; grep cannot tell you who is about to edit a file. Pass region_start/region_end to lock only some lines; shared locks allow concurrent readers. If another agent holds it the reply names them (or force=true steals it and records a conflict). The TTL (default 300 s) is renewed by your heartbeats, so pick it for a stretch without heartbeats, not for the whole task. retry=true waits with backoff (at most 600 s).

document_path.description: Path to the document to lock

lock_type.description: 'exclusive' (default) blocks all other locks on overlapping regions. 'shared' allows concurrent shared locks.

force.description: Steal the lock if held by another agent

retry.description: Retry with exponential backoff on lock contention (default: False)

backoff_ms.description: Starting backoff in milliseconds for retry (default: 100)

timeout_ms.description: Total timeout in milliseconds for retry (default: 5000)

region_start.description: Start line of the region to lock (omit for whole-file lock)

region_end.description: End line of the region to lock (omit for whole-file lock)

release_lock.description: Release your lock as soon as your edit of a shared file is done. reason 'expired' means the TTL ran out before this call (expired_at says when; locked_by names any new holder): nothing was released, and you should check the file before relying on your lock. Pass region_start/region_end for a region lock.

agent_id.description: Agent releasing the lock (must be the owner)

region_start.description: Start line of the region to lock (omit for whole-file lock)

region_end.description: End line of the region to lock (omit for whole-file lock)

refresh_lock.description: Extend one lock's TTL (or change it) without releasing it. heartbeat already renews all your locks under half their TTL; use this to give one lock a longer TTL. reason 'expired' means it ran out first: acquire_lock again.

agent_id.description: Agent refreshing the lock (must be the owner)

region_start.description: Start line of the region to lock (omit for whole-file lock)

region_end.description: End line of the region to lock (omit for whole-file lock)

get_lock_status.description: Before editing a shared file, check whether someone holds it and until when. Returns every active lock on the path, including region locks.

list_locks.description: See every active lock, or one agent's (agent_id): which shared files are taken and by whom, with expiry times. Use it to pick work that does not collide.

agent_id.description: Optional agent ID to filter locks by holder

force_refresh.description: If true, re-warm the in-memory cache from SQLite before reading. Default false.

admin_locks.description: Clean-up for coordinators. action='release_by_agent' drops all of one agent's locks (released counts live ones, expired lists ones that had run out); 'reap_expired' clears expired locks; 'reap_stale' marks agents without a recent heartbeat stopped and drops their locks.

agent_id.description: Agent whose locks to release (required for release_by_agent)

timeout.description: Seconds after which an agent is stale (default: 600)

broadcast.description: Tell your live sibling agents what you are about to do before an action that affects them (changing a shared API, say). With handoff_targets it records a formal handoff; with require_ack it tracks who acknowledged.

document_path.description: Optional document path to check for lock conflicts

ttl.description: Staleness cutoff for sibling detection in seconds (default: 30)

handoff_targets.description: Explicit list of agent IDs to hand off to. When provided, broadcast becomes a formal multi-recipient handoff recorded in the handoffs table and sends messages to each target.

require_ack.description: If True, require recipients to acknowledge the broadcast via acknowledge_broadcast

message.description: Optional message payload when require_ack is True

acknowledge_broadcast.description: Answer a broadcast_ack_request message you received, so the sender's wait_for_broadcast_acks can finish.

broadcast_id.description: ID of the broadcast to acknowledge

wait_for_broadcast_acks.description: After broadcast with require_ack=true, wait until every recipient acknowledged or the timeout passes. Waits at most 600 s whatever the timeout; a capped reply has wait_capped_s.

broadcast_id.description: ID of the broadcast to wait for

wait_for_locks.description: Wait until other agents release the given files, then edit them, instead of polling get_lock_status. Returns released and still-locked paths. Waits at most 600 s whatever the timeout; a capped reply has wait_capped_s.

document_paths.description: List of document paths to wait on

await_agent.description: Wait until another agent deregisters (finishes), when your next step depends on its work. Waits at most 600 s whatever the timeout; a capped reply has wait_capped_s.

notify_change.description: After changing a shared file, record it so other agents see it in get_notifications (and know to re-read it).

get_notifications.description: Check what other agents changed, locked or unlocked since a time (since), or long-poll with timeout_s as an idle wait (it answers as soon as something arrives, at most 600 s; timed_out says nothing came). Pass agent_id as yourself to also get locks_expiring (your locks under half their TTL: heartbeat renews them) and locks_expired (ran out). prune_* options delete old rows first.

agent_id.description: You: adds your expiring and expired locks to the reply

timeout_s.description: Long-poll timeout in seconds (0 = answer at once; at most 600)

get_conflicts.description: Look up lock steals, refused locks and ownership crossings, for example to find out why a lock was refused or who overwrote whom.

document_path.description: Filter to a specific document path

agent_id.description: Filter to conflicts involving this agent

limit.description: Maximum number of conflicts to return

get_contention_hotspots.description: Find the files agents fight over most (ranked by lock conflicts), to split work or plan the order of edits on them.

limit.description: Maximum number of hotspots to return

status.description: One-call summary of the hub: agent, lock, notification and conflict counts, and whether a coordination graph is loaded.

load_coordination_spec.description: Reload the coordination spec from disk. Returns whether a graph was found and loaded, plus the graph's agent list.

path.description: Path to coordination_spec.yaml or .json (default: project root)

scan_project.description: Perform a file ownership scan of the worktree_root. For every tracked file (.py, .md, .json, .yaml, .txt, .toml), upserts an entry into the file_ownership table. Returns the count of files scanned and owned.

worktree_root.description: Root directory to scan (default: engine's project root)

extensions.description: File extensions to scan (default: py, md, json, yaml, txt, toml)

get_agent_status.description: Get full status for a specific agent: current task, responsibilities (from the coordination graph), owned files, lineage, and lock state.

get_file_agent_map.description: Get a map of all tracked files to their assigned Agent ID and responsibility summary. Returns the full file_ownership table joined with agent responsibilities.

agent_id.description: Filter to files owned by a specific agent

update_agent_status.description: Update the current task description and/or declared scope for an agent. Stored in agent_responsibilities for visibility. Scope is a list of path prefixes that define the agent's working domain. If an agent declares a scope, lock acquisitions outside that scope are denied.

current_task.description: Human-readable description of what this agent is doing

scope.description: List of path prefixes defining the agent's scope (e.g. ['/src/services/', '/src/models/'])

run_assessment.description: Run an assessment suite or score the current live session. If suite_path is provided, loads the JSON suite file and scores it. If suite_path is omitted, synthesizes a live session trace from DB state (agents, notifications, lineage) — no hand-authored suite required. Stores results in SQLite and returns a Markdown or JSON report.

suite_path.description: Path to the JSON test suite file (omit for live session scoring)

graph_agent_id.description: Optional: filter traces to those involving this graph agent role

scope.description: 'project' (default) restricts to the current worktree; 'all' scores every agent in the DB

get_agent_tree.description: See the whole swarm at once: who spawned whom, what each agent is doing, which files each has locked, and boundary warnings. Start here when you join a project already in progress.

agent_id.description: Root of the tree to query (default: oldest active root agent)

send_message.description: Ask or tell one specific agent something (an API question, a handoff note). The recipient reads it with manage_messages action='get'.

payload.description: Optional JSON payload. Serialized JSON is truncated to MAX_MESSAGE at the primitive (T6.14) so a bloated payload can't corrupt storage.

caller_agent_id.description: Optional caller assertion (T2.4). When supplied, must equal from_agent_id — rejects impersonation where a compromised caller forges a message 'from' another agent.

manage_messages.description: Read your messages (action='get', unread_only to filter), mark them read (mark_read), or send one (send). Check after registering and between steps.

action.description: Messaging action. 'send' requires from/to/message_type. 'get' and 'mark_read' only need agent_id.

since_id.description: Return only messages with id > since_id (cursor for incremental polling, action='get')

caller_agent_id.description: Optional caller assertion (T2.4). For send, must equal from_agent_id; for get/mark_read, must equal agent_id. Blocks cross-agent impersonation / inbox siphoning.

create_task.description: Put a piece of work on the shared board so an agent can claim it (assign_task). depends_on orders tasks.

depends_on.description: Task IDs that must complete before this one starts

priority.description: Task priority (higher values execute first; default 0)

assign_task.description: Claim a task before working on it (assign it to yourself) so no other agent takes it. Refused when another agent holds it: the reply names the holder. force=true reassigns on purpose.

assigned_agent_id.description: Agent to assign the task to

force.description: Reassign even if another agent holds the task

update_task_status.description: Report progress on a task you hold: in_progress, completed (with a summary) or failed (with an error).

summary.description: Completion summary written by the agent (used for compression chains)

blocked_by.description: Task ID that is blocking this task

error.description: Error message when marking a task as failed (records to dead letter queue)

query_tasks.description: Read tasks: one by id (task), those you created (child), those assigned to an agent (by_agent), all, a task's subtasks, or its tree.

task_id.description: Task ID (required for query_type='task'; omit otherwise)

parent_agent_id.description: Agent ID (required for query_type='child'; omit otherwise)

assigned_agent_id.description: Agent ID (required for query_type='by_agent'; omit otherwise)

parent_task_id.description: Parent task ID (required for query_type='subtasks'; omit otherwise)

root_task_id.description: Root task ID (required for query_type='tree'; omit otherwise)

create_subtask.description: Create a subtask under an existing parent task. The subtask inherits context from its parent and can be nested further. Use get_task_tree to retrieve the full hierarchy.

parent_task_id.description: ID of the parent task this subtask belongs to

depends_on.description: Task IDs that must complete before this subtask starts

priority.description: Subtask priority (higher values execute first; default 0)

wait_for_task.description: Wait until a task is completed or failed, when your work depends on it. Waits at most 600 s whatever the timeout; a capped reply has wait_capped_s.

get_available_tasks.description: Find work to pick up: pending tasks whose dependencies are completed. unassigned_only=true leaves out tasks someone already claimed.

agent_id.description: Optional agent ID to filter to tasks assigned to this agent

unassigned_only.description: Only tasks nobody is assigned to: what an idle agent can claim

manage_work_intents.description: Announce which files you plan to touch soon (declare), see others' plans (get), or withdraw yours (clear). Lighter than a lock: it warns others when they lock those files.

action.description: Intent action. 'declare' requires document_path and intent. 'get' / 'clear' only need agent_id.

document_path.description: File path the intent targets (required for declare)

wait_for_handoff.description: Wait until a handoff is completed (mode='completion', the default), or read its record (mode='status'). To act on a handoff use acknowledge_handoff, complete_handoff or cancel_handoff; the older modes 'ack', 'complete' and 'cancel' still work here. Waits at most 600 s whatever the timeout; a capped reply has wait_capped_s.

acknowledge_handoff.description: Acknowledge a handoff addressed to you. The handoff can be completed once every recipient has acknowledged it.

handoff_id.description: Handoff ID (from broadcast with handoff_targets, or the handoff message payload)

complete_handoff.description: Mark a handoff completed. Refused until every recipient has acknowledged it.

cancel_handoff.description: Cancel a handoff that is no longer needed.

manage_dependencies.description: Unified dependency management. mode='declare' creates a dependency. mode='check'/'blockers'/'assert' queries blockers. mode='satisfy' marks one satisfied. mode='list' lists all. mode='wait' polls until a dep_id is satisfied.

task_failures.description: Unified dead-letter queue operations. action='retry' resurrects a task. action='list_dead_letter' lists DLQ tasks. action='history' gets failure history for a task.

acquire_coordinator_lease.description: Attempt to acquire the coordinator leadership lease (COORDINATOR_LEADER). If acquired, this agent becomes the active coordinator.

agent_id.description: Agent ID attempting to acquire the lease

manage_leases.description: Unified lease management. action='acquire' | 'refresh' | 'release' | 'get' (returns current leader; agent_id not needed) | 'claim' (failover claim). agent_id is required for every action but 'get'.

ttl.description: TTL for acquire/claim (seconds, default 10 at the engine)

spawn_subagent.description: Register intent to spawn a sub-agent and return its spawn ID. The parent agent calls this before the external system spawns the sub-agent. This creates a pending spawn record that the spawning system will consume when the agent is actually spawned, correlating via ``parent_agent_id``. Returns the spawn ID and pending spawn record.

parent_agent_id.description: Parent agent ID that intends to spawn the sub-agent

prompt.description: Prompt or instructions for the sub-agent

source.description: Source system that will perform the spawn (e.g. 'stdio_adapter')

report_subagent_spawned.description: Report that a sub-agent has been spawned by an external system. Any IDE/CLI (stdio_adapter, etc.) calls this after spawning a sub-agent via its native mechanism. This consumes the pending spawn record created by ``spawn_subagent`` and links it to the actual child agent ID.

parent_agent_id.description: Parent agent ID that spawned the sub-agent

subagent_type.description: Type of sub-agent that was spawned

child_agent_id.description: Actual agent ID of the spawned sub-agent

source.description: Source system that performed the spawn (e.g. 'stdio_adapter')

caller_agent_id.description: Optional caller assertion (T2.4). When supplied, must equal parent_agent_id — rejects sibling agents trying to claim another parent's child and hijack the spawner.registered event.

get_pending_spawns.description: Get pending (or all) spawn requests for a parent agent. Returns spawn records with status: pending | registered | expired.

parent_agent_id.description: Parent agent ID to get pending spawns for

await_subagent_registration.description: After spawn_subagent, wait until the spawned agent registers. Returns the consumed spawn record, or timed_out. Waits at most 600 s whatever the timeout; a capped reply has wait_capped_s.

parent_agent_id.description: Parent agent ID that spawned the sub-agent

subagent_type.description: Wait for a specific sub-agent type (omit to wait for any)

request_subagent_deregistration.description: Request graceful deregistration of a child agent. Sets ``stop_requested_at`` on the child agent. The child is expected to poll ``is_subagent_stop_requested`` and call ``deregister_agent`` if the stop flag is set. After a timeout, the caller should escalate to ``deregister_agent`` directly. Returns ``requested`` if the stop flag was set, ``not_found`` if the child agent does not exist or is not active.

parent_agent_id.description: Parent agent ID making the request

child_agent_id.description: Child agent ID to request stop for

is_subagent_stop_requested.description: Check if a stop has been requested for this agent. The agent should call this periodically and deregister if the stop flag is set.

agent_id.description: Agent ID to check stop-request flag for

await_subagent_stopped.description: After request_subagent_deregistration, wait until the child stops. timed_out with escalate=true means call deregister_agent for it yourself. Waits at most 600 s whatever the timeout; a capped reply has wait_capped_s.

child_agent_id.description: Child agent ID to wait for
